chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, appointed Ali (peace be upon him) as a flag between Him and His creatures. So whoever recognized him was a believer, and whoever denied him was a disbeliever, and whoever was ignorant of him was astray, and whoever appointed anything with him was a polytheist, and whoever came with his Wilayah entered Paradise, and whoever came with his animosity entered the Fire.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of recognizing Imam Ali in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) elevates the recognition of Ali’s Wilayah to the status of a divine sign (‘alam) that serves as the primary criterion for faith, framing it as the axis around which Islamic theology revolves. It presents a comprehensive typology of spiritual states—linking knowledge, denial, ignorance, and shirk directly to the Imam’s authority—thereby establishing Wilayah not merely as a political claim but as the essential key to entering Paradise and avoiding Hell.
